description: We are a team of storytellers, dreamers, and space enthusiasts exploring the forgotten side of space exploration. Through TARS Protocol, we bring NASA's abandoned and discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars back into the spotlight, imagining the untold stories behind these forgotten machines. Blending science, creativity, and cinematic storytelling, we aim to give a voice to the machines left behind and uncover the stories still waiting to be told.
summary:
The Things We Left Behind

Team: TARS PROTOCOL

The Things We Left Behind is a cinematic, story-driven documentary exploring two remarkable machines left behind on other worlds: the Apollo 17 Lunar Roving Vehicle on the Moon and NASA's Spirit rover on Mars.

Through scientific facts, historical footage and emotional narration, we bring their journeys to life. We explore how the Lunar Roving Vehicle helped astronauts navigate the Moon and collect valuable geological samples, revealing clues about its ancient history.

Our journey then takes us to Mars, where Spirit, originally designed for a 90-Martian-day mission, continued exploring for over six years. We highlight its discoveries of silica-rich deposits and carbonate-bearing rocks, providing evidence of ancient water-related environments and clues about Mars' potential habitability.

Beyond scientific achievements, our documentary celebrates human curiosity, innovation and determination. Though these machines are no longer active, their discoveries continue to shape our understanding of the Solar System.

Countless other spacecraft, rovers and instruments remain across different worlds, but we focus on just two stories. Through The Things We Left Behind, TARS PROTOCOL reminds viewers that even when a mission ends, its legacy lives on.
details: We made a documentry covering two abandoned space machines by nasa. We brought them back to life again. The intend of the project is to make sure that these technologies are not forgotten as their missions are over. It shows the impact and findings made by these machines. We used image and videos from nasa's image library and youtube. Musics are downloaded from non-copyrighted sources. The SI usage is very minimal. Our team wanted to build a cinematic experience. A documentry that could make viewers go "wow".
